sources.name: Kenney (kenney.nl), CC0 1.0
sources.terms: Five audio packs by Kenney: Sci-fi Sounds, Impact Sounds, Interface Sounds, UI Audio and Digital Audio. Each pack page lists the licence as "Creative Commons CC0" and each archive contains a License.txt that names CC0 1.0 (http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) and says the content may be used in personal, educational and commercial projects. Credit is welcome but not required; it is given here anyway. The pack pages carry a robots meta tag with "noai" and a "tdm-reservation" marker. The files are used here as ordinary game sound material and for listening tests, not as training data for any model; if that ever changes, ask Kenney first. The .url shortcut files in the archives are not unpacked.

sources.name: NASA, public domain in general
sources.terms: Recordings hosted on nasa.gov and its subdomains (www.nasa.gov, images-assets.nasa.gov). NASA's media usage guidelines (https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/) say that NASA content, audio included, "generally" is not subject to copyright in the United States, may be used without explicit permission when used factually and without implying endorsement, and that NASA should be acknowledged as the source. What matters for this game: (1) the game must not suggest that NASA endorses it or any product; (2) the NASA insignia, logos and emblems are not part of these files and must not be used without clearance; (3) a recording with an identifiable person, and that includes the voice of an astronaut or flight controller, is covered by the privacy and publicity rights of that person when used commercially, and current NASA astronauts and employees may not appear in commercial or promotional products at all; the speech files are therefore test material for the radio filter and for listening, and are not to be shipped in the game without a separate decision; (4) third-party material that NASA shows on its pages keeps its own rights; nothing of that kind was taken. Where a NASA page names someone besides NASA in the credit, the credit is recorded exactly: "NASA/University of Iowa" for the plasma wave recordings (the page states no restriction beyond NASA's guidelines), "Courtesy of the EMFISIS team at the University of Iowa" for the chorus recording, "NASA/JPL-Caltech/SwRI/Univ of Iowa" for Juno, and the long Mars credits for Perseverance SuperCam. Pages read: https://www.nasa.gov/historical-sounds/, https://www.nasa.gov/sounds-from-beyond/, https://www.nasa.gov/artemisaudio/ ("All audio files are free to download and cleared for use in accordance with NASA's media usage guidelines."), https://www.nasa.gov/history/apollo-11-audio-highlights/, https://www.nasa.gov/missions/mms/nasa-listens-in-as-electrons-whistle-while-they-work/ and the NASA Image and Video Library.
